Detailed Description

A Code D7571 occurs when the Drive Controller detects a voltage less than 9.1 volts on the un-switched power supply from the battery. If Code D7571 occurs, the drive functions will be disabled.

  • Supply wire 1250 or 1260 shorted to ground or open.
  • Ground wire 2040 or 2490 open.
  • Battery.
  • Alternator.
  • Drive Controller.

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

D7518 - Right Swash Plate Not In Neutral

Detailed Description

A Code D7518 occurs when the Drive Controller detects the Right Swash Plate sensor is not in the neutral range of 2.08 – 2.92 volts. When the PTOL is enabled, the Drive Controller will monitor the position of the Swash Plate sensors. The Swash Plate sensors are located at the bottom of the pump and are keyed to the swash plate inside the pump. Swash Plate sensors provide feedback to the Drive Controller on the position of the swash plate inside the pump. The Swash Plate sensor is supplied battery voltage from the Gateway Controller, but the Swash Plate output signal range is 1.0 to 4.0 volts. This code will only occur at the system start up, not during normal operation. If a Code D7518 occurs, the engine will shutdown.

Possible Causes

  • Contamination of the hydraulic system.
  • Hydraulic pump is not physically centered. Refer to the Service Manual.
  • Right Swash Plate sensor.
  • Drive Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive Controller connectors, Swash Plate sensor connector, or SJC wire harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Cycle power.

D7527 - Left Swash Plate Out Of Position

Detailed Description

A Code D7527 occurs when the Drive / Drive Plus Controller detects the Left Swash Plate position is opposite of the commanded position. The code also occurs during operation when the Drive / Drive Plus Controller expects the swash plate to be in neutral and the sensor feedback is not in the neutral range of 2.08 – 2.92 volts. When the PTOL button is pressed with the seat bar down, the Drive / Drive Plus Controller will look at the position of the Swash Plate sensors and continue to monitor them during operation. If a Code D7527 occurs, the engine will shutdown. The Swash Plate sensors are located at the bottom of the pump and are keyed to the swash plate inside the pump. The Swash Plate sensors are supplied battery voltage from the Gateway Controller, but the Swash Plate output signal range is 1.0 to 4.0 volts. These sensors provide feedback on the position of the swash plate to the Drive / Drive Plus Controller.

Possible Causes

  • Contamination of the hydraulic system.
  • Hydraulic pump is not physically centered. Refer to the Service Manual.
  • Left Swash Plate sensor.
  • Left Drive solenoids not properly connected.
  • Left Forward Drive solenoid or Left Reverse Drive solenoid shorted to supply voltage or ground. Check for additional error codes D7543, D7544, D7553, D7554, and D7575.
  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, Swash Plate sensor connector, or AWS / SJC wire harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

D7591 - Left Swash Plate Sensor - Reversed

Detailed Description

A Code D7591 occurs when the Drive / Drive Plus Controller detects that the left wheel / track movement is in the same direction as the joystick position and the Left Swash Plate sensor is indicating wheel / track movement in the opposite direction. When the PTOL button is pressed with the seat bar down, the Drive / Drive Plus Controller will look at the position of the Swash Plate sensors and continue to monitor them during operation. If a Code D7591 occurs, the machine will continue to operate in Speed Management Mode. The Swash Plate sensors are located at the bottom of the pump and are keyed to the swash plate inside the pump. The Swash Plate sensors are supplied battery voltage from the Gateway Controller, but the output signal range is 1.0 to 4.0 volts. The Swash Plate sensors provide feedback to the Drive Plus Controller on the position of the swash plate inside the pump. If the "Swashplate FB" is being viewed in Service Analyzer/Diagnostics, the bars on the graphs will move in opposite directions when drive is commanded, when there are no Swash plate codes present.

Possible Causes

  • Left Swash Plate sensor installed incorrectly – sensor shaft 180˚ out of position.
  • Left and right swash plate connections reversed.
  • Signal wires 3810 (or 4720) and 3860 (or 4950) reversed.
  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, or wire harness connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. A Code D7592 occurs when the Drive / Drive Plus Controller detects that the right wheel / track movement is in the same direction as the joystick position and the Right Swash Plate sensor is indicating wheel / track movement in the opposite direction. When the PTOL button is pressed with the seat bar down, the Drive / Drive Plus Controller will look at the position of the Swash Plate sensors and continue to monitor them during operation. If a Code D7592 Code occurs, the machine will operate in Speed Management Mode. The Swash Plate sensors are located at the bottom of the pump and are keyed to the swash plate inside the pump. The Swash Plate sensors are supplied battery voltage from the Gateway Controller, but the output signal range is 1.0 to 4.0 volts. The Swash Plate sensors provide feedback to the Drive Plus Controller on the position of the swash plate inside the pump. If the "Swashplate FB" is being viewed in Service Analyzer/Diagnostics, the bars on the graphs will move in opposite directions when drive is commanded, when there are no Swash plate codes present.

Possible Causes

  • Right swash plate sensor installed incorrectly – sensor shaft 180˚ out of position.
  • Left and right swash plate connections reversed.
  • Signal wires 3810 (or 4720) and 3860 (or 4950) reversed.
  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, or wire harness connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Cycle power.

W3251 - ACS Lift Actuator Short To Battery (Error On) (ACS Only)

Detailed Description

A Code W3251 occurs when the ACS Controller detects the voltage from the Lift Actuator, signal wire 4620, is greater than 4.9 volts. The ACS Controller supplies 5.0 volts to the Lift Actuator sensor. If a Code W3251 occurs, the lift and tilt functions will be disabled.

Possible Causes

  • Lift Actuator needs calibrating.
  • 5 volt supply wire 5980 shorted to supply voltage.
  • Signal wire 4620 shorted to supply voltage.
  • Ground wire 2670 open.
  • Lift Actuator.
  • ACS Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the ACS Controller connectors, Lift Actuator connector, or ACS harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Cycle power.

Detailed Description

  • Motor wire 4600 or 4610 shorted to ground.
  • Signal wire 4620 shorted to ground or open.
  • 5 volt supply wire 5980 shorted to ground or open.
  • Lift Actuator.
  • ACS Controller.

  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

W3268 - ACS Lift Handle Information Error

Detailed Description

A Code W3268 indicates a CAN communication error between the Drive Controller and the ACS Controller. This code is only displayed with an SJC machine and only while in H-Pattern. The position of the Left Joystick is monitored by the Drive Controller. While in H-Pattern, the X-axis (side to side motion) values must be transferred to the ACS Controller via the CAN communication wires. If code W3268 occurs Drive, Lift, and Tilt functions will be disabled.

Possible Causes

  • Damaged SJC wire harness.
  • CAN communication wires 95xx or 96xx.
  • Loss of power to the Drive Controller.
  • Drive Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the ACS Controller connectors and Drive Controller connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

In Hand Mode, wire 4450/4550 does not provide battery voltage to the ACS Controller. In Foot Mode, wire 4450/4550 provides battery voltage to the ACS Controller. If a Code W3267 occurs, the lift and tilt functions will be disabled.

Possible Causes

  • Operator toggled the Hand/Foot mode selection switch after PTOL was enabled.
  • Signal wire 4450/4550 shorted to supply voltage, shorted to ground, or open.
  • Supply wire 1785 shorted to ground or open.
  • Hand/Foot selection mode switch.
  • ACS Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the ACS Controller connectors, Hand/Foot mode selection switch, ACS wire harness, Cab harness, or Mainframe harness Connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. W4007 - Right CAN Joystick Y-axis Not In Neutral

Detailed Description

A Code W4007 occurs when the ACS Controller detects the Right Joystick Y-axis is not in neutral when PTOL is enabled. This code can only occur in ISO Mode. If a Code W4007 occurs, the lift and tilt functions will be disabled. If the door is not fully latched or if the door is opened and closed during operation, this code may occur. If operating with Remote Control and a Code W4007 occurs, use Service Analyzer\Diagnostics\Radio Remote Control Diagnostics to verify correct operation of the Right Joystick.

  • Door sensor (ISO Mode only).

long_description:
E000132-00 - MAF Plausibility HIGH Fault

Detailed Description

If a Code P00BD occurs, the ECU does not detect proper ground on the MAF sensor. Air tube between MAF and intake being loose or not connected can also cause this code to occur.The Intake Air Flow (MAF) sensor converts the amount of air drawn into the engine into a voltage signal. The primary components of the Intake Air Flow(MAF) sensor are a thermistor, a platinum hot wire, and an electronic control circuit. The thermistor measures the temperature of the incoming air. The hot wire is maintained at a constant temperature in relation to the thermistor by the electronic control circuit. An increase in air flow will cause the hot wire to lose heat faster and the electronic control circuitry will compensate by sending more current through the wire. The electronic control circuit simultaneously measures the current flow and puts out a voltage signal in proportion to the current flow. The voltage will decrease as the air flow increases.If a Code P00BD occurs, the engine will be de-rated 25%.For a Code P00BD to occur, the condition must be detected for 3 seconds.If an open circuit to ground is detected, you may also see code E000172-03and E000132-03

Possible Causes

  • Open circuit on pin 120
  • Air tube leak between MAF and Intake
  • Intake Air Flow (MAF) sensor.
  • Engine Controller.
  • Loose Pin to Socket fit in connector
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Engine ECU connectors, Mass Air Flow sensor connector, Engine to Mainframe harness connector, Mainframe harness, or the Engine harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Engine running.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Resolution of Condition found above
title: E000132-00

M6402 - Switched Power Relay Error On

Detailed Description

A Code M6402 occurs when the Gateway Controller detects voltage on wire 3450 when not commanded. The Switched Power relay supplies voltage to the HVAC relay and the circuits attached to Fuses FRC1 Fuse 1, FRC1 Fuse 2, FRC1 Fuse 3, FRC1 Fuse 4, FRC1 Fuse 5, FRC1 Fuse 7, FRC1 Fuse 8, or FRC1 Fuse 12 . This code will only occur at start up, and is only displayed in Service Analyzer.

Possible Causes

  • Feedback wire 3450 shorted to supply voltage.
  • Circuits controlled by Fuses FRC1 Fuse 1, FRC1 Fuse 2, FRC1 Fuse 3, FRC1 Fuse 4, FRC1 Fuse 5, FRC1 Fuse 7, FRC1 Fuse 8, or FRC1 Fuse 12 shorted to supply voltage.
  • Switched Power relay.
  • Gateway Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Gateway Controller connectors, Auxiliary Controller connectors, ACS Controller connectors, Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, Switched Power relay connector, Mainframe harness, ACS harness, AWS / SJC harness, Engine harness, or Cab harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Cycle power.

M1017 - Hydraulic Charge Filter Plugged

Detailed Description

A Code M1017 occurs when the Gateway Controller detects that the Hydraulic Charge Filter switch is open for 30 seconds while the engine is running and the hydraulic charge oil is above 130˚F. The Hydraulic Charge Filter switch is a normally closed switch that mounts to the back of the Hydraulic Charge Fan filter assembly. The switch is grounded through the filter housing. The Hydraulic Charge Filter switch will open when the difference of hydraulic pressure across the filter reaches a critical level. When the switch opens, the Gateway Controller detects that the filter is plugged.

Possible Causes

  • Plugged hydraulic charge filter.
  • The Hydraulic Charge Filter switch is not grounded through the filter housing during operation.
  • Signal wire 3440 is open.
  • Hydraulic Charge Filter switch.

long_description:
The DCU checks whether the dosing valve is physically blocked by checking whether the pressure drops normally by opening the dosing valve with the pressure in the pressure line at 5 bar.
If a blockage is detected, the state is left with error and the counter is incremented. If the counter exceeds the maximum acceptable number of repetitions the fault is set.
If the pressure line and the dosing valve are blocked, the pressure will not drop below threshold (4300hPa) for longer than (7s).

long_description:
In February 2018 Service Analyzer version 86.2 implemented two new codes (M0144 and M0145) related to air filter plugging for Loaders with M4 Gateway Controllers (M4 Gateway was introduced in summer 2016 in preparation for M2 Loader production). 
The same changes were implemented for Bobcat Engine Loaders equipped with the older Gateway controllers in June 2018 with Service Analyzer version 86.10.

Air Filter Plugged Engine Protection De-rate Strategy:
The engine power derate strategy was designed to allow plenty of warning to the machine operator before reducing available power. It is also implemented in such a way that an air filter change will immediately restore full engine performance.  

Logic:

  • Time stamp of machine hours recorded when M0117 is first displayed.
  • Time stamp is cleared if 8 machine hours pass without another M0117.
  • Each time another M0117 occurs the time between the first and the current M0117 is calculated. If greater than 8 hours then code M0144 is displayed instead of M0117 (if timestamp is not reset)
  • Code M0145 is displayed if 16 hours is measured between first and subsequent M0117 (if time stamp is not reset).

 
M0144:

  • Engine speed and torque derate level 1
  • 25% torque derate, 2000 max RPM
  • Can finish the job, but slow

 
M0145:

  • Engine speed and torque derate level 2
  • 60% torque derate
  • Limp mode / trailer loading

 
Key Cycle:

  • Time stamp is kept during key off
  • Derate stops, but resumes with the next M0117 until time stamp is cleared
  • Enables immediate return to full power when air filter is changed
short_description: Air Filter Plugged / Air Filter Derate Level 1 / Air Filter Derate Level 2
title: M0117 / M0144 / M0145

Description:
  If a Code E000097-31 occurs, the ECU detects the presence of water in the Fuel Filter for approx. 5 seconds.
  The water in fuel sensor determines the presence of water in the fuel by measuring the conductivity of the fluid. As the water level in the fuel filter/water separator increases, the resistance across the WIF sensor decreases. This decrease in resistance is sent as a signal to the Engine Controller and compared to a standard reference value. The WIF sensor is a two wire sensor and is supplied 5.0 volts from the ECU.
  Resistance across pins of sensor should be 75k-4.6 M when in Fuel
  Machine may go into de-rate after sensing water for extended period of time

Possible Cause:

Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Description:
  A Code M6202 occurs when the Gateway Controller detects an electrical problem with the Tailgate Fan.
 

The fault detection for this output from the controller is a pullup detection, when the output is off the resistance or the fan motor pulls the detection signal down, so if the fuse is blown creating an open circuit to the controller pin (no load), it will code M6202.  

If Code M6202 occurs, the Tailgate Fan may be running when not commanded or may not run when commanded.

Code: M0217: Hydraulic/hydrostatic Filter Plugged
Description:
  A Code M0217 occurs when the Gateway Controller detects the Hydraulic Implement Filter switch signal wire is open for 30 seconds while the engine is running, and the hydraulic oil temperature is above 130˚F. The Hydraulic Implement Filter switch is a normally closed switch that is mounted to the back of the filter assembly. The switch opens when the hydraulic pressure through the Hydraulic Implement Filter reaches a critical level, and allows the hydraulic oil to bypass the filter.
Possible Cause:
  • Hydraulic Implement Filter.
  • Signal wire or ground wire open.
  • Hydraulic Implement Filter switch.
  • Gateway Controller.

Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures.
Conditions for Code:
  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

long_description:
Overview

Code P0254 - E001076-16 will be active if there is a delay in the rail pressure reaching the expected pressure level requested by the ECU. This code will often appear with code P0002 - E000157-21. Code P0087 - E000157-10 is also set in a similar manner - usually during extended cranking when rail pressure won't reach demand. Troubleshooting any of these faults is the same. 

 

CODE

POSSIBLE CAUSES

EFFECT

E001076-16
  1. Low Pressure side fuel (no fuel in tank, fuel leakage before HP pump, fuel filter plugged, fuel line clogging, sucking air at a line connection or loose fuel filter)
  2. High pressure side problem (injector stuck open, faulty HP pump, IMV sticking, leaking faulty, high pressure pipe leaking, rail pressure sensor bad.)
  3. Electric problem (IMV connector, Wiring harness IMV to ECU)

  Check Engine Indicator Flashing

  Torque Reduction (Lvl 1)

  Delay engine stop

  Engine may not start

 

Condition for Running Diagnostic

P0254 - E001076-16  Key on and engine running (including cranking)

P0002 - E000157-21: Key on and engine running

P0087 - E000157-10: Key on and engine cranking

Condition for Setting the Fault Code

P0254 - E001076-16: If the current of IMV trim value is lower than the threshold, fault code is raised.

P0002 - E000157-21: If the resistance of IMV (feedback) is out of the threshold during restricted condition, fault code is raised within 1 second.

P0087 - E000157-10: If rail pressure does not build within time threshold, fault code is raised.

Condition for Clearing the Fault Code

P0254 - E001076-16: If the current of IMV trim value is within the threshold, fault code is cleared

P0002 - E000157-21: If the resistance of IMV (feedback) is within the threshold during restricted condition, fault code is cleared within 1 second.

P0087 - E000157-10: If rail pressure builds within the time threshold, fault code is cleared.
short_description: Rail Pressure Control or Build-up Fault
title: P0002 - E000157-21 / P0254 - E001076-16 / P0087 - E000157-10

If a Code M8402 occurs, the DCU sends a CAN message it will enter the DESOX mode. Every 200 operating hours the DCU will initiate a passive DESOX which notifies the operator to continue operating the machine under a load for approximately 15 minutes or longer. A Code H1224 occurs when the Auxiliary Controller detects that the Front Auxiliary Thumb Paddle switch is not in neutral when the auxiliaries are enabled. If a Code H1224 occurs, the Front Auxiliary outputs will be disabled. For Manual and ACS controlled machines, the normal neutral voltage range on signal wire 4320 is 3.5 - 4.5 volts. The voltage is varied depending on the position of the Right Thumb Paddle switch, and is sent to the Auxiliary Controller on signal wire 4320. The switch is supplied 8.0 volts from the Auxiliary Controller on wire 4300. For AWS / SJC Loaders, CAN communication, wires 91xx/95xx and 92xx/96xx, send the information from the Right Thumb Paddle switch to the Auxiliary Controller. If operating with Remote Control and a Code H1224 occurs, use Service Analyzer\Diagnostics\Radio Remote Control Diagnostics to verify correct operation of the Front Auxiliary Thumb Paddle switch.

Possible Causes

  • Operator holding Front Auxiliary Thumb Paddle switch out of neutral when enabling auxiliaries.
  • 8 volt supply wire 4300 shorted to battery voltage.
  • Signal wire 4320 shorted to supply voltage.
  • Right handle (Manual / ACS only).
  • Right CAN joystick grip (AWS/SJC only).

Detailed Description

A Code H1221 occurs when the Auxiliary Controller detects that the Front Auxiliary Thumb Paddle switch has traveled outside of its normal left directional limit. For Manual and ACS controlled machines, a Code H1221 occurs when the Auxiliary Controller detects a voltage greater than 7.55 volts on the Right Thumb Paddle switch, signal wire 4320. The voltage is varied depending on the position of the Right Thumb Paddle switch, and is sent to the Auxiliary Controller on signal wire 4320. The switch is supplied 8.0 volts from the Auxiliary Controller on wire 4300. For AWS / SJC Loaders, a Code H1221 occurs when the Auxiliary Controller detects the Right Thumb Paddle switch is out of range. CAN communication, wires 91xx/95xx and 92xx/96xx, send the information from the Right Thumb Paddle switch to the Auxiliary Controller.

Possible Causes

  • Incorrect wiring of the Right Handle 10-pin connector (Manual / ACS only).
  • Signal wire 4320 shorted to supply voltage (Manual / ACS only).
  • Ground wire 4310 open (Manual / ACS only).
  • Right Handle (Manual / ACS only).
  • Right CAN joystick grip (AWS/SJC only).
  • Auxiliary Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Auxiliary Controller connectors, Right Handle connector, Right CAN Joystick Grip connector, or Mainframe harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.

long_description:
U003516-01 - DEF Quality Error - Concentration too low

Detailed Description

A code U003516-00 or U003516-01 will appear when the sensor detects DEF solution concentration outside of the allowable limit for 10 minutes continuously. Based on the amount of time this code is displayed you may go into repeat offense mode. This can lead to various stages of engine de-rate. Various sequences of icon blink and buzzer will occur, refer to the Service Manual for further information.Stages of engine de-rate: Warning Stage No de-rateStage 1 25% engine torque de-rateStage 2 50% engine Stage 3 Machine will Idle onlyOnce the code is cleared, it may take up to 30 minutes of engine runtime to reach full engine rpm and torque (slowly ramps up by 10 rpm increments)

Possible Causes

  • DEF concentration is outside the 32.5% +/- tolerance
  • Air in DEF fluid
  • Debris on tip of sensor
  • Sensor out of specification
  • *NOTE: Due to tolerance in the sensor, it may read different than handheld refractometers

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch on

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Key switch on.
short_description: DEF Quality Error - Concentration too low

long_description:
D7579 - Left Speed Sensor Out Of Range Low

Detailed Description

A Code D7579 will occur when the Drive Controller detects that the pulses from the Left Speed sensor are less than 0.15 volts. This information is used by the Drive Controller to detect machine movement and speed. If a Code D7579 occurs, the machine will operate in Speed Management Mode. A wheel machine has sensors in the motor carriers that detect magnets on a rotating disk. A track machine has sensors in the drive motors that detect the teeth on a metal sprocket.

Possible Causes

  • Signal wire (3080 or 3885) or signal wire (3020 or 3880) shorted to ground.
  • 5 volt supply wire 5880 shorted to ground or open.
  • Left Wheel Speed sensor.
  • Drive Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive Controller connectors or SJC harness connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Self Resetting.
short_description: Left Speed Sensor Out Of Range Low
title: D7579

If in ISO Mode or on an AWS machine, the Backup Alarm is activated when the Left Joystick is pulled backward. If in H-Pattern, the Backup Alarm is activated when the Left and Right Joysticks are pulled backward.

Possible Causes

  • Signal wire 7100 shorted to a supply voltage.
  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, AWS / SJC wire harness, Mainframe wire harness, or Backup Alarm harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

long_description:
D7594 - Unresponsive Left Speed Sensor

Detailed Description

A Code D7594 occurs when the Drive / Drive Plus Controller detects that there is a command from the Joystick for machine movement and the Left Swash Plate sensor is in the correct position but there is no speed detected from the Left Speed sensor for 18 seconds. This information is used by the Drive / Drive Plus Controller to detect machine movement and speed. The Wheel Speed sensors are located in the motor carriers that detect magnets on a rotating disk. The Track machine sensors are located in the drive motors that detect the teeth on a metal sprocket.

Possible Causes

  • Supply wire 5880, ground 2880 or signal wire (3020 or 3880) or (3080 or 3885) open.
  • Metal particles on the speed sensor or magnetic disc.
  • Wheel / Track Speed sensor or magnetic disc.
  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, speed sensor connector, or wire harness connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Cycle power.
title: D7594

long_description:
D7517 - Left Swash Plate Not In Neutral

Detailed Description

A Code D7517 occurs when the Drive Controller detects the Left Swash Plate sensor is not in the neutral range of 2.08 – 2.92 volts. When the Press To Operate Loader (PTOL) is enabled, the Drive Controller will monitor the position of the Swash Plate sensors. The Swash Plate sensors are located at the bottom of the pump and are keyed to the swash plate inside the pump. The Swash Plate sensor is supplied battery voltage from the Gateway Controller, but the Swash Plate output signal range is 1.0 to 4.0 volts. This code will only occur at the system start up, not during normal operation. If a Code D7517 occurs, the engine will shutdown.

Possible Causes

  • Contamination of the hydraulic system.
  • Hydraulic pump is not physically centered. Refer to the Service Manual.
  • Left Swash Plate sensor.
  • Drive Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive Controller connectors, Swash Plate sensor connector, or SJC wire harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

  • Cycle power.

A Code M7504 occurs when the Gateway Controller does not have communication with the Drive / Drive Plus Controller. The Gateway Controller communicates with the Drive / Drive Plus Controller through CAN communication.

Possible Causes

  • CAN communication wires 91xx/93xx or 92xx/94xx open.
  • Supply wires 1250 or 1260 open.
  • Ground wires 2040 or 2490 open.
  • Gateway Controller.
  • Drive / Drive Plus controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Gateway Controller connectors, Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, AWS/SJC harness, or the Mainframe harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Cycle power.
title: M7504

M0216 - Hydraulic Implement Filter Not Connected

Detailed Description

A Code M0216 occurs when the Gateway Controller detects an open circuit for 30 seconds on the Hydraulic Implement Filter switch, signal wire 3320, at Key switch / (run/enter) On. The Hydraulic Implement Filter switch is a normally closed switch that is mounted to the back of the filter assembly. The switch opens when the hydraulic pressure through the Hydraulic Implement Filter reaches a critical level, and allows the hydraulic oil to bypass the filter. A Code M0216 may occur while the engine is running if the open was present before the engine was started.

Possible Causes

  • Signal wire 3320 or ground wire 2320 open.
  • Hydraulic Implement Filter switch.
  • Gateway Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Gateway Controller connectors, Hydraulic Implement Filter switch connector, or Mainframe harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

M1910 - Engine Ambient Temperature High

Detailed Description

If A Code M1910 occurs, the Gateway Controller detects that the Engine Compartment temperature is at least 197°F for 3 minutes. The Engine Ambient Temperature sensor has an operating range of 950 to 4400 ohms. As the air temperature increases, the resistance of the sensor and the voltage on the signal wire decreases.

Possible Causes

  • Machine being operated in extreme heat environment.
  • Obstruction blocking normal flow of air.
  • Gateway Controller.
  • ECU Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Gateway Controller connectors, Engine Controller connectors, Engine to Mainframe harness connector, Engine harness, or the Mainframe harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.

Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. A Code M6728 occurs when the Gateway Controller detects an internal fault with the HVAC Output. The HVAC Output is the signal provided by the Gateway Controller to energize the HVAC Relay.
